test_method: generate_preset (write) -> describe_preset (readback) against live Serum 2.0.21 via serum-mcp runtime

results.match: PARTIAL - integer inputs match exactly (5->5); fractional inputs truncate in DISPLAY only (1.5->2, 7.3->7)
results.classification: LIVE_EXECUTION_VERIFIED (write proven); LIVE_READBACK_VERIFIED UNPROVEN for fractional rates (describe_preset summary truncates to integer, cannot confirm raw fractional storage via this tool)
results.root_cause: describe_preset()'s human-readable text summary formats LFO rate as integer; this is a display-layer limitation in serum-mcp's own tool, not confirmed to be a mapping.py/introspect.py data bug
results.action_required: Raw CBOR/binary inspection needed to confirm fractional LFO rate is correctly stored (out of scope for describe_preset-based verification); OR flag fractional LFO rate readback as MANUAL_REQUIRED until a better verification path exists

results.match: PARTIAL - type confirmed; kParamTimeL/kParamTimeR/kParamBeatSync NOT shown in describe_preset summary (only type+wet surfaced)
results.classification: LIVE_EXECUTION_VERIFIED (type only); LIVE_READBACK_VERIFIED for FX sub-parameters UNPROVEN via this tool (summary too coarse)
results.action_required: FX sub-parameter readback needs a finer-grained verification path than describe_preset's summary

critical_findings.finding_1: describe_preset() summary is a HUMAN-READABLE TEXT REPORT, not a full structured readback API — it omits/rounds many fields (LFO rate precision, FX sub-parameters, oscillator engine-specific fields beyond the basics). This limits its use as a LIVE_READBACK_VERIFIED mechanism to only the fields it actually prints.
critical_findings.finding_2: 6 of 8 mechanisms (oscillator, filter, envelope, matrix, arp, global) show CLEAN write+readback match on the fields describe_preset displays.
critical_findings.finding_3: 2 of 8 mechanisms (LFO rate precision, FX sub-parameters) require a DIFFERENT verification approach — describe_preset's summary format is insufficiently granular. This does NOT mean the underlying mapping.py write is broken; it means THIS verification tool can't confirm it.
critical_findings.finding_4: No live Serum 2.0.21 GUI visual verification was performed (no screenshot/UI confirmation) — describe_preset reads the WRITTEN PRESET FILE, not Serum's loaded/rendered state. True LIVE_READBACK_VERIFIED per the original PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ARCHITECTURE.md definition (UI/raw state proves value was set) requires loading the preset in Serum's actual UI, which was not done here.

revised_terminal_state_definitions.note: Given finding_4, even the 6 'clean matches' above are more accurately: FILE_WRITE_VERIFIED (preset file contains expected value, confirmed via serum-mcp's own describe_preset reader) — NOT full LIVE_READBACK_VERIFIED (which requires Serum's actual GUI/plugin state, not just the file serum-mcp wrote and re-read with its own parser).
revised_terminal_state_definitions.implication: This is a MEANINGFUL BUT PARTIAL proof: it confirms the write path + describe_preset's parse path agree with each other. It does NOT yet confirm Serum 2.0.21 itself interprets the file correctly when loaded live. True proof requires: open preset in Serum UI (via computer-use or screenshot) and visually confirm control positions.
